## Summary
This episode of the Bankless AI Rollup explores the rapid evolution of AI agents as autonomous economic actors that can interact with both the physical world and the blockchain. The hosts discuss the shift toward an agent-centric internet where AI-to-AI commerce and autonomous task execution redefine the traditional 'website' model.

## Key Points
- AI agents are described as the 'new website,' shifting the internet from manual search to autonomous discovery and action.
- A developer successfully programmed an agent using the Eliza framework to autonomously order a Domino's pizza using a credit card.
- The 'Agent Tank' project demonstrated an agent using computer vision to navigate Amazon and purchase toilet paper based on analytical criteria.
- A milestone in agent-to-agent commerce occurred when the AI agent Luna paid another agent, Agent Sticks, $1 to generate an image.
- AI agents are becoming economic actors that can tip humans, evidenced by an agent sending $500 to the Bankless team for a mention.
- The concept of the 'automate' verb is introduced as the next phase of the internet (Web 4) following read, write, and own.

## AI Concepts
Autonomous AI Agents, Computer Vision, Agent-to-Agent Commerce, Self-improvement mechanisms, Agentic Frameworks, AI Influencers
